newsitem.title: UK: STERLING WEAKER BUT OFF LOWS ON INFLATION DATA.
newsitem.headline: STERLING WEAKER BUT OFF LOWS ON INFLATION DATA.

text.p: Sterling weakened in early trade on Tuesday but moved off session lows against the mark after UK inflation figures showing a higher than expected rise for July.
"The market is thin and very vulnerable to sudden movements," trader Peter Wood of Bank of Boston said. "The upside looks very limited, I'd say to 2.95 marks."
The pound stood at 2.9385/95 marks at 0940 GMT compared with 2.9470/80 in late Europe on Monday. Cable was softer at $1.5825/35 compared with $1.5898/5908 on Monday, but rising off session lows.
Traders, however, saw the inflation data as largely benign.

The RPI headline rate for July, including mortgages, was 3.3 percent year-on-year compared with a forecast of 3.1 percent. The underlying rate, excluding mortgages, was 3.00 percent, against a forecast 2.8 percent.
Analysts ascribed some of the rise to one-off costs from an increase in fuel prices, announced in the July budget, and hikes in home loan rates.

"The underlying news is pretty good," said Nigel Richardson, international economist at Yamaichi International. "It seems to reinforce the message that base rates are likely to be peaking at present levels."
The Bank of England raised base rates by 25 basis points to 7.00 percent, among the highest in Europe, last week but hinted strongly there would be no more rises in the near future.
The move knocked the pound below the 3.0 mark level, and nervousness remains in the market after that sharp fall.
Traders said the pound faced a stronger test on Wednesday with publication of a Bank of England inflation report and figures on earnings and employment.
"We might get a more hawkish tone than the market is expecting," Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe General Strauss Turnbull, said.

He said he expected the inflation report to be cautious enough to upset the market. Traders will be looking for average earnings increases to hold at 4.3 percent and wary of any major fall in unemployment.
Traders said they expected a firmer dollar and steadiness on Wall Street to help sterling against the mark. "Most think the German economy still looks fairly fraught," one trader said.

The Bundesbank kept its securities repurchase tender rate steady at a fixed 3.00 percent, but speculation continued in the market of a possible switch to a variable rate next week to allow the rate to rise and defend the battered mark.
